definition: Tortuous means full of twists and turns.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word tortuous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know tortuous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Lost tourists often give up on the old quarter's tortuous cobblestone alleys, which bend, fork, and loop back on themselves every few steps.
A crooked path has a few bends in it; a tortuous one twists and turns constantly along its whole length.
A labyrinthine route is even more extreme than a tortuous one, so tangled that it feels like a maze designed to trap you.

Winding means curving gently along its course, the way a river winds through a valley; the curves are easy, even pleasant. Tortuous means twisting relentlessly, tight turn after tight turn, until the twisting itself becomes the obstacle.

Serpentine means twisting like a snake, in smooth, continuous S-curves, and the word often admires the shape, as in a serpentine garden path. Tortuous has no admiration in it: a tortuous route twists so constantly and so tightly that following it becomes a trial.

Meandering means following a slow, wandering course with no hurry and no plan, like a meandering stream or a meandering conversation; the word is relaxed. Tortuous is punishing: its endless tight turns and doubling back frustrate anyone actually trying to get somewhere.

Tortuous means full of twists and turns.
The trail through the slot canyon was so tortuous that hikers lost sight of one another around every bend, and the route folded through a dozen tight turns in a single mile.
The trail constantly bends, folds, and turns rather than running straight, so hikers can never see far ahead.
A path defined by that endless twisting is exactly what tortuous describes.
Tortuous usually describes routes: a tortuous road, path, river, or trail.
Be careful not to confuse it with torturous, which means 'causing torture or great pain'; a tortuous lane merely twists, while a torturous hike leaves you in agony.
Tortuous can also describe overly complicated arguments or procedures, but its core image is always literal winding.

The narrow-gauge railway that once served the silver mines climbs the gorge on a famously tortuous line.
Engineers could find no straight route up the canyon walls, so the track coils through forty-one numbered curves in nineteen miles.
Some loops turn so tightly that the locomotive crew can look across and see the tail of their own train on the track below.
Passengers hoping for a quick trip learn patience; the constant turning holds the train to fifteen miles an hour.
Modern highways bypass the gorge entirely, but the old line survives as a heritage run for travelers who want the twisting itself.
